name: Munich Airport
direct_access_note: First-hand browser access to www.munich-airport.com: 9 pages captured on desktop and mobile, 13 more read with Playwright, 4 interaction scripts; all HTTP 200, no bot challenge. Blocked by the container's network policy (not site defects): code.etracker.com (analytics), cdn.eye-able.com (Visual help toolbar), www.munich-airport.de (German site and host of the embedded digital map), parken.munich-airport.de (parking booking engine). The digital map, the Visual help tool, the chatbot widget and the parking checkout were therefore not observable. Captures were taken about 01:00 local time, so only the statuses 'planned' and 'departed' were live. Scores are expert assessments, not instrumented tests.

steps_to_flight_status_note: Homepage flight module: type flight number, press SEARCH; result row appears inline with status, times and area. Requires scrolling to the module first; one more click opens the detail page with the gate.
axe_note: Homepage, axe-core WCAG A/AA rule violations. Departures page: desktop 9 (critical 4, serious 4, moderate 1), mobile 12 (critical 5, serious 6, moderate 1).

lighthouse_lab.note: lab, single container, third-party hosts blocked, indicative only

standouts.name: Login-free flight tracking strip
standouts.why: One toggle pins a flight under the header on every page using browser storage; no account or app needed.

standouts.name: Inline flight search on the homepage
standouts.why: Airport, airline and flight-number autocomplete with results rendered in place and a four-week schedule.

standouts.name: Rich flight detail page
standouts.why: Joins gate, check-in area, airline contact, weather at both ends and aircraft facts on one page.

standouts.name: Site search with typeahead and flight-intent routing
standouts.why: Section-labelled results; 'prayer room' returns the four right facilities first; flight-like queries go to flight search.

standouts.name: Operationally detailed accessible-travel content
standouts.why: PRM codes, notification rules, Sunflower programme and accessible checkpoint, promoted as a homepage quick link, with a published accessibility declaration.

weaknesses: Technical accessibility: 10-13 axe rule violations per page with 4-6 critical, Lighthouse accessibility 47, pinch zoom disabled, no visible skip link, airline logos without alt text
Flight status is plain lower-case text with no colour or icon; no alerts beyond the on-page strip; no live security waiting times
Digital map is consent-gated on a second domain and the map page has no fallback list or plan when it does not load
Only two languages (English, German) for an intercontinental hub
Commerce stops at parking: no online shop or reserve-and-collect; lounge and VIP services by PDF or offline
ideas: Keep the login-free tracking idea but add opt-in web push or WhatsApp alerts and a colour-plus-icon status system that works for colour-blind users
Put the flight search field in the first viewport on mobile and desktop, ahead of campaign imagery
Ship a first-party, consent-free map with step-free routing, walking times and a 'show on map' link on every facility page
Make accessibility measurable: zero critical axe findings as a release gate, a visible skip link and a strong focus ring
Answer destination and flight-number queries in site search with a live flight card instead of press releases
Join parking, lounge and fast-track in one basket tied to the tracked flight
gaps: Digital map, Visual help toolbar, chatbot widget and parking checkout not observable (blocked hosts or consent gating)
Only 'planned' and 'departed' statuses were live; delay, cancellation and boarding treatments unverified
Absence of a passenger app is inferred from the site and one inconclusive search, not confirmed in app stores
Lighthouse and capture timings are lab values from one container with analytics blocked
